newsitem.title: UK: Don't inflame tension, Britain's PM tells Israel.
newsitem.headline: Don't inflame tension, Britain's PM tells Israel.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major warned Israel's leaders on Wednesday not to inflame tension by expanding Jewish settlements in disputed areas.

"In the current tense atmosphere ... it will be all the more important for both sides to avoid anything that could be construed as provocation," Major told a dinner attended by senior figures with links to Israel.

"The question of Israeli settlements is again becoming urgent. It is hard to see how the reports of settlement expansion there and of the renewed financial incentives can do other than inflame the situation," he warned.
Israel decided last week to grant financial befefits to Jewish settlers in Arab areas, a move which heightened tension between Israel and the Palestinians.
Major also urged the Israeli government and the Palestinian Liberation Organisation (PLO) to agree quickly on the handover of 80 percent of Hebron to Palestinian self-rule.

The handover was promised in a peace deal more than a year ago, but the partial withdrawal of Israeli troops has not yet taken place because the two sides have been unable to settle on security arrangements for some 400 Jews living in the heart of Hebron, amid more than 100,000 Arabs.

"It is vital that such an agreement be concluded urgently not only for its own sake, but because it will restore the faith of the man on the street, be he in Tel Aviv or Gaza, that the peace process lives," said Major.
